([[Waterford Township, Michigan|Waterford, Michigan]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 22 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team3 = [[Los Angeles Clippers]] | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Defensive Team (2021) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2021) }} '''Isaiah Ju'mar Jackson''' (born January 10, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the first round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. ==High school career== As a freshman, Jackson played basketball for Lutheran Northwest High School in [[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]. He moved to Old Redford Academy in [[Detroit]] for his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Isaiah Jackson commits to Kentucky, video highlights 'making it out' of Pontiac |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/11/isaiah-jackson-commits-to-kentucky-video-highlights-making-it-out-of-pontiac.html |website=MLive |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=November 16, 2019}} As a junior, Jackson competed for SPIRE Academy in [[Geneva, Ohio]] alongside [[LaMelo Ball]] and his Old Redford teammate [[Rocket Watts]].{{cite web |last1=Goricki |first1=David |title=Waterford Mott's Isaiah Jackson, a top MSU target, returns as nation's No. 3 power forward |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/06/18/waterford-motts-isaiah-jackson-returns-nations-no-3-power-forward/1493556001/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=June 18, 2019}} He averaged 14.9 points and 10.4 rebounds per game. For his senior season, he transferred to [[Waterford Mott High School]] in [[Waterford Township, Michigan|Waterford, Michigan]].{{cite web |last1=Purcell |first1=Jared |title=Finally home, 5-star Isaiah Jackson lifts Waterford Mott basketball to new level |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/12/finally-home-5-star-isaiah-jackson-lifts-waterford-mott-basketball-to-new-level.html |website=MLive |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=December 13, 2019}} Jackson averaged 19.1 points, 13 rebounds and 7.7 blocks per game as a senior.{{cite web |last1=Tucker |first1=Kyle |title=His anger channeled, Isaiah Jackson is already turning heads at Kentucky |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2220466/2020/11/25/his-anger-channeled-isaiah-jackson-is-already-turning-heads-at-kentucky/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} He was named to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |last1=Moore |first1=Deb |title=Four UK MBB Signees Selected for Jordan Brand Classic Game |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2020/2/16/mens-basketball-four-uk-mbb-signees-selected-for-jordan-brand-classic-game |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=May 8, 2021 |date=February 16, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], Jackson committed to playing college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Kentucky Wildcats get commitment from No. 22 recruit Isaiah Jackson |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/28093703/kentucky-wildcats-get-commitment-no-22-recruit-isaiah-jackson |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 8, 2021 accessdate = May 9, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On December 1, 2020, Jackson recorded seven points, 12 rebounds and a career-high eight blocks in a 65–62 loss to seventh-ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] at the [[Champions Classic]]. He had the most single-game blocks by a Kentucky player since [[Willie Cauley-Stein]] in 2013.{{cite web |title=Kentucky-Kansas Postgame Notes |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2020/12/2/mens-basketball-kentucky-kansas-postgame-notes.aspx |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=May 9, 2021 |date=December 2, 2020}} As a freshman, Jackson averaged 8.4 points, 6.6 rebounds and an [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]-high 2.6 blocks per game, earning SEC All-Defensive and All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |title=Isaiah Jackson named to SEC All-Freshman and All-Defensive teams |url=https://www.wymt.com/2021/03/09/isaiah-jackson-named-to-sec-all-freshman-and-all-defensive-teams/ |website=[[WYMT-TV]] |access-date=May 9, 2021 |date=March 9, 2021}} On March 17, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |title=Kentucky Wildcats' Isaiah Jackson to test NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31084155/kentucky-wildcats-isaiah-jackson-test-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 9, 2021 |date=March 17, 2021}} He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Kentucky freshman Isaiah Jackson, ESPN's No. 11 prospect, to keep name in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31526712/kentucky-freshman-isaiah-jackson-espn-no-11-prospect-keep-name-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 30, 2021 |date=May 28, 2021}} ==Professional career== Jackson was selected with the 22nd pick of the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and then traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Pacers Acquire Isaiah Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-isaiah-jackson |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 6, 2021 |date=August 6, 2021}} On October 23, he made his NBA debut, scoring one point in two minutes of action during a 102–91 overtime win over the [[2021–22 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=BRISSETT HELPS PACERS PULL AWAY FROM HEAT IN OVERTIME |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100028 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 31, 2022, Jackson logged a career-high 26 points, alongside ten rebounds and two blocks, in a 122–116 win over the [[2021–22 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |title=JACKSON'S BREAKOUT GAME SENDS PACERS PAST CLIPPERS 122-116 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100760 |access-date=January 22, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He made 36 appearances (including 15 starts) for Indiana during his rookie season, averaging 8.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Jackson 2021–22 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432170/type/nba/year/2022|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Jackson played in 63 contests (including 12 starts) for the Pacers during the [[2022–23 NBA season]], averaging 7.2 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Jackson 2022–23 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432170/type/nba/year/2023|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 59 appearances (three starts) for Indiana in the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], logging averages of 6.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Jackson 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432170/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Jackson [[Achilles tendon rupture|tore his Achilles tendon]] on November 1, 2024 against the [[2024–25 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]], ending his season.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2024-11-03 |title=Pacers lose center Jackson to torn Achilles |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42150111/sources-pacers-isaiah-jackson-suffers-torn-achilles-tendon |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} Prior to the injury, he had averaged 7.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.0 assist over five appearances (one start). On July 11, 2025, Jackson re-signed with the Pacers on a three-year, $21 million contract.{{cite web|title= Indiana Pacers Re-Sign Isaiah Jackson |url= https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-re-sign-isaiah-jackson |website=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2025|access-date=July 11, 2025}} Jackson made 38 appearances (14 starts) for the Pacers during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 6.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Jackson 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432170/isaiah-jackson|access-date=February 11, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On February 5, 2026, Jackson, [[Bennedict Mathurin]], two first-round picks and one second-round pick were traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Ivica Zubac]] and [[Kobe Brown]].{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS ACQUIRE MATHURIN, JACKSON AND TWO FIRST-ROUND PICKS FROM INDIANA |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-acquire-mathurin-jackson-and-two-first-round-picks-from-indiana |access-date=2026-02-06 |date=2026-02-05 |website=NBA.com
